packages.setup:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    mkdir ${_kernel}
    bsdtar-static -xf %(sourcedir)/ajantv2.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C ${_kernel}

    pushd ${_kernel}
    # This is where patches would go
    # Linux 7.2 removed strncpy() in favor of strscpy().
    # https://github.com/aja-video/libajantv2/commit/434ea72bca772275100ec0556cf4a53d5a3494f6
    # TODO: Remove in next update
    %patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-linux-driver-fix-compile-with-kernel-7.2.patch
    popd
done
packages.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}/driver
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make -C linux \
        KDIR="%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/build" \
        KVERSION="${_kernel}" \
        LLVM=1
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
packages.install:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %install_file driver/bin/ajantv2.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/drivers/aja/
    %install_file driver/bin/ajardma.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/drivers/aja/

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
packages.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    kernels+=(${dir##*/})
done

# plugin) are dropped because their configuration is not stateless: auditd
# reads the plugin directory from /etc/audit/plugins.d and audisp-remote
# reads /etc/audit/audisp-remote.conf, neither of which falls back to

%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless.patch

%reconfigure \
    --disable-gssapi-krb5 \
    --disable-legacy-actions \
    --disable-static \
    --disable-zos-remote \
    --with-io_uring \
    --with-libcap-ng \
    --with-nftables \
    --with-python3 \
    --with-vendordir=%(vendordir)

   %(installroot)%(sbindir)/audisp-remote \
   %(installroot)%(mandir)/man5/audisp-remote.conf.5 \
   %(installroot)%(mandir)/man8/audisp-filter.8 \
   %(installroot)%(mandir)/man8/audisp-remote.8

# No dispatcher plugins are enabled by default
rm %(installroot)%(sysconfdir)/audit/audisp-filter.conf \
   %(installroot)%(sysconfdir)/audit/audisp-remote.conf
rm -r %(installroot)%(sysconfdir)/audit/plugins.d

# System config is admin-owned; the shipped defaults live in %(vendordir)
%tmpfiles "# Audit daemon"
%tmpfiles "d /etc/audit 0750 root root -"
%tmpfiles "d /etc/audit/plugins.d 0750 root root -"

packages.install:
# Construct a shared initrd containing the bcachefs/mkfs/fsck bins.
#  We do this hear because we need to copy additional libs into the initrd,
#  and those libs ABSOLUTELY MUST be ABI compatible with the libraries in the
#  base initrd. The safest way to achieve that is to create the initd here
#  instead of in the bcachefs-tools build. By doing this the bcachefs tools
#  initrd is guaranteed to be rebuilt immediately after the root initrd is
#  built, guaranteeing ABI compatibility.
%install_dir initrd/%(libdir)/systemd/system-generators
%install_exe %(sbindir)/bcachefs initrd/%(sbindir)/bcachefs
%install_file %(udevrulesdir)/64-bcachefs.rules -t initrd/%(udevrulesdir)/
ln -srv initrd/%(sbindir)/bcachefs initrd/%(libdir)/systemd/system-generators/bcachefs-mount-generator
for i in fsck.bcachefs mount.bcachefs; do
    ln -srv initrd/%(sbindir)/bcachefs initrd/%(sbindir)/${i}
done

# We need to copy in the libs that are needed to run the binary
function copy_or_symlink() {
    file=$1

    if test -h %(libdir)/${file}; then
        link=$(readlink %(libdir)/${file})

        ln -s ${link} initrd/%(libdir)/${file}
        copy_or_symlink ${link}
    else
        cp -a %(libdir)/${file} initrd/%(libdir)/${file}
    fi
}

readarray -t libs <<<"$(${READELF} -d %(sbindir)/bcachefs | grep "NEEDED" | awk '{print $5}' | sed -e 's|\[||g' -e 's|]||g')"
for i in ${libs[@]}; do
    case $i in
        # We know for sure these are in the root initrd. Many of the rest are as well
        #  but there's very little space wasted by including duplicates
        libzstd.so.1|libz.so.1|libgcc_s.so.1|libc.so.6|ld-linux-x86-64.so.2)
            continue
            ;;
        *)
            copy_or_symlink ${i}
            ;;
    esac
done

pushd initrd
find . -exec touch -d @0 --no-dereference {} \;
find . | cpio -o -H newc --device-independent --reproducible | zstd -19 -T0 -c > ../bcachefs-tools.initrd
popd
%install_file bcachefs-tools.initrd %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/initrd.d/65-%(name)-shared.initrd

for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %install_file src/fs/bcachefs/bcachefs.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/fs/bcachefs

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Create an initrd for .ko files
    mkdir -p initrd/%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/fs/bcachefs
    find %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules -name '*.ko' -exec cp -v {} initrd/%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/fs/bcachefs \;
    touch initrd/.dracut-depmod-invalidate
    pushd initrd
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/${_kernel}
    find . -exec touch -d @0 {} \;
    find . | cpio -o -H newc --device-independent --reproducible | zstd -19 -T0 -c > %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/${_kernel}/70-%(name)-%(version).initrd
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done

packages.name: bison
packages.description:
Bison is a general-purpose parser generator that converts an annotated context-free grammar into a deterministic LR or generalized LR (GLR) parser employing LALR(1) parser tables. As an experimental feature, Bison can also generate IELR(1) or canonical LR(1) parser tables. Once you are proficient with Bison, you can use it to develop a wide range of language parsers, from those used in simple desk calculators to complex programming languages.

Bison is upward compatible with Yacc: all properly-written Yacc grammars ought to work with Bison with no change. Anyone familiar with Yacc should be able to use Bison with little trouble. You need to be fluent in C or C++ programming in order to use Bison. Java is also supported as an experimental feature.

packages.setup:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    # Debian patches require the source in a certain structure. We imitate that structure even though we don't build for i386
    mkdir -p ${_kernel}/amd64 ${_kernel}/i386
    bsdtar-static -xf %(sourcedir)/broadcom.tar.gz --strip-components=0 -C ${_kernel}/amd64
    bsdtar-static -xf %(sourcedir)/broadcom.tar.gz --strip-components=0 -C ${_kernel}/i386

    pushd ${_kernel}

    # This is basically a hack so that the Debian patches apply cleanly. This file is not installed
    cp %(sourcedir)/README.txt README.txt

    # Also a hack for compat with 01-shipped-module.patch
    mv amd64/lib/wlc_hybrid.o_shipped amd64/lib/wlc_hybrid.o_amd64

    if [[ -f %(pkgdir)/patches/series ]]
    then
        # This retains patch order while removings blank lines
        # and lines starting with a # character (with any number of preceding blanks)
        # which should make the patch series file nicer to maintain due to comment support
        PATCHES=($(sed -E -e '/^\s*$/d' -e '/^[[:space:]]*#.*$/d' %(pkgdir)/patches/series))
        for p in "${PATCHES[@]}"
        do
            %patch "%(pkgdir)/patches/${p}"
        done
    fi

    # Might as well delete the i386 directory since we don't need it
    rm -rf i386
    popd
done
packages.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}/amd64
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make LLVM=1 KBASE="%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}" KERNELRELEASE=${_kernel}
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
packages.install:
%install_file %(pkgdir)/modprobe.conf %(installroot)%(libdir)/modprobe.d/broadcom-wl.conf

for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}/amd64
    %install_file wl.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/wireless/

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
packages.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    kernels+=(${dir##*/})
done

packages.install:
%cmake_install

# Setup ccache symlinks for gnu and clang compilers
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(libdir)/ccache/bin
TGT="%(installroot)/%(libdir)/ccache/bin"
for compiler in \
    clang \
    clang++ \
    clang-20 \
    clang++-20 \
    clang-21 \
    clang++-21 \
    clang-22 \
    clang++-22 \
    clang-23 \
    clang++-23 \
    gcc \
    g++ \
    c++ \
    cc \
    x86_64-aerynos-linux-gcc \
    x86_64-aerynos-linux-g++ \
    x86_64-aerynos-linux-c++ \
    x86_64-aerynos-linux-cc \
    x86_64-solus-linux-gcc \
    x86_64-solus-linux-g++ \
    x86_64-solus-linux-c++ \
    x86_64-solus-linux-cc \
    ; do
    ln -sv /usr/bin/ccache "${TGT}/${compiler}"
done

# Install our default config
%install_file %(pkgdir)/ccache.conf %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/ccache/ccache.conf

ddcutil is a program for querying and changing monitor settings, such as brightness and color levels.

ddcutil uses DDC/CI to communicate with monitors implementing MCCS (Monitor Control Command Set) over I2C. Normally, the video driver for the monitor exposes the I2C channel as devices named /dev/i2c-n. There is also psupport for monitors (such as Apple Cinema and Eizo ColorEdge) that implement MCCS using a USB connection.

A particular use case for ddcutil is as part of color profile management. Monitor calibration is relative to the monitor color settings currently in effect, e.g. red gain. ddcutil allows color related settings to be saved at the time a monitor is calibrated, and then restored when the calibration is applied.

packages.name: docbook
packages.summary: Markup schema, suitable for writing technical books and documentation
packages.description: %(name) is a schema (available in several languages including RELAX NG, W3C XML Schemas, and XML DTDs) maintained by the DocBook Technical Committee of OASIS. It is particularly well suited to books and papers about computer hardware and software (though it is by no means limited to these applications).
packages.install:
## Setup the catalog
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/docbook/docbook-dtd/

xml_catalog="%(installroot)/%(vendordir)/docbook/docbook-dtd/catalog"
xmlcatalog --noout --create "$xml_catalog"

for ver in 4.1.2 4.2 4.3 %(version); do
    mkdir docbook-xml-${ver}
    unzip -d docbook-xml-${ver} %(sourcedir)/${ver}.zip

    pushd docbook-xml-${ver}
    %install_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xml-dtd-${ver}
    cp -dr docbook.cat *.dtd ent/ *.mod %(installroot)/%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xml-dtd-${ver}

    # Inspired by Arch
    case $ver in
        4.1.2) xml=' XML' ;;&
        *)
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//DTD DocBook XML V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/docbookx.dtd" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//DTD DocBook$xml CALS Table Model V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/calstblx.dtd" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//DTD XML Exchange Table Model 19990315//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/soextblx.dtd" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ELEMENTS DocBook$xml Information Pool V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/dbpoolx.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ELEMENTS DocBook$xml Document Hierarchy V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/dbhierx.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ENTITIES DocBook$xml Additional General Entities V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/dbgenent.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ENTITIES DocBook$xml Notations V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/dbnotnx.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ENTITIES DocBook$xml Character Entities V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/dbcentx.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            ;;&
        4.[45])
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "public" \
                "-//OASIS//ELEMENTS DocBook XML HTML Tables V${ver}//EN" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}/htmltblx.mod" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            ;;&
        *)
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "rewriteSystem" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}" \
                "/usr/share/xml/docbook/xml-dtd-${ver}" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            xmlcatalog --noout --add "rewriteURI" \
                "http://www.oasis-open.org/docbook/xml/${ver}" \
                "/usr/share/xml/docbook/xml-dtd-${ver}" \
                "$xml_catalog"
            ;;&
    esac
done

packages.name: docbook-xsl
packages.description: XML stylesheets for Docbook-xml transformations
packages.setup:
for i in docbook-xsl-nons docbook-xsl-ns; do
    pushd $i
    %patch %(pkgdir)/no-stack-overflow.patch
    popd
done
packages.install:
for i in nons ns; do
    case $i in
        nons) ns="-nons" ;;
        ns) ns="" ;;
    esac
    versioned_dir="xsl-stylesheets$ns-%(version)"
    destdir="%(installroot)/%(datadir)/xml/docbook/$versioned_dir"

    pushd docbook-xsl-$i
    install -Dt "$destdir" -m644 VERSION{,.xsl}
    (
    shopt -s nullglob
    for fn in assembly common eclipse epub epub3 fo highlighting html \
        htmlhelp javahelp lib manpages params profiling roundtrip template \
        website xhtml xhtml-1_1 xhtml5
    do
        install -Dt "$destdir/$fn" -m644 $fn/*.{xml,xsl,dtd,ent}
    done
    )

    popd
    # Unversioned directory for compatibility
    ln -sv $versioned_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xsl-stylesheets$ns
done

## Catalog
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/docbook/docbook-xsl/
xml_catalog="%(installroot)/%(vendordir)/docbook/docbook-xsl/catalog"
xmlcatalog --noout --create "$xml_catalog"

for v in %(version) current; do
    for x in rewriteSystem rewriteURI; do
        xmlcatalog --noout --add $x \
            "http://cdn.docbook.org/release/xsl/$v" \
            "%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xsl-stylesheets-%(version)" \
            "$xml_catalog"
        xmlcatalog --noout --add $x \
            "http://cdn.docbook.org/release/xsl-nons/$v" \
            "%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xsl-stylesheets-nons-%(version)" \
            "$xml_catalog"
        xmlcatalog --noout --add $x \
            "http://docbook.sourceforge.net/release/xsl-ns/$v" \
            "%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xsl-stylesheets-%(version)" \
            "$xml_catalog"
        xmlcatalog --noout --add $x \
            "http://docbook.sourceforge.net/release/xsl/$v" \
            "%(datadir)/xml/docbook/xsl-stylesheets-nons-%(version)" \
            "$xml_catalog"
    done
done

packages.name: dracut
packages.summary: dracut is an event driven initramfs infrastructure.
packages.description:
dracut (the tool) is used to create an initramfs image by copying tools and files from an installed system and combining it with the dracut framework, usually found in /usr/lib/dracut/modules.d.
Unlike other implementations, dracut hard-codes as little as possible into the initramfs. The initramfs has (basically) one purpose in life -- getting the rootfs mounted so that we can transition to the real rootfs. This is all driven off of device availability. Therefore, instead of scripts hard-coded to do various things, we depend on udev to create device nodes for us and then when we have the rootfs's device node, we mount and carry on. This helps to keep the time required in the initramfs as little as possible so that things like a 5 second boot aren't made impossible as a result of the very existence of an initramfs.
Most of the initramfs generation functionality in dracut is provided by a bunch of generator modules that are sourced by the main dracut script to install specific functionality into the initramfs. They live in the modules.d subdirectory, and use functionality provided by dracut-functions to do their work.

%patch %(pkgdir)/0001-solus-Add-module-to-invalidate-depmod-index.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/0002-Support-stateless-glibc-ldconfig-configuration.patch

# https://www.mail-archive.com/initramfs@vger.kernel.org/msg01700.html
%patch %(pkgdir)/0004-Create-ldconfig-folder-in-initramfs.patch

%patch %(pkgdir)/0005-solus-Allow-for-skipping-firmware-installation.patch

# https://github.com/dracut-ng/dracut/pull/2781
%patch %(pkgdir)/2781.patch

# Uses bash syntax: ./configure: 26: [[: not found
%configure_with_bash

find %(installroot)%(mandir) -empty -type d -delete

. edksetup.sh

# Shell
for _ARCH in ${_BUILD_ARCHS[@]}; do
    # Shell not currently used
    # echo "Building shell for ${_ARCH}"
    # BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build \
    #     -p ShellPkg/ShellPkg.dsc \
    #     -a "${_ARCH}" \
    #     ${_CC_OPTS[@]}

    case "${_ARCH}" in
        AARCH64)
            echo "Building ArmVirtPkg ($_ARCH) with secure boot support"
            _build_options=(
                -p ArmVirtPkg/ArmVirtQemu.dsc
                -a "$_ARCH"
                "${_CC_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_EFI_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_NETWORK_TLS[@]}"
                -D SECURE_BOOT_ENABLE
            )
            BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build "${_build_options[@]}"
            dd if=/dev/zero of=Build/ArmVirtQemu-AArch64/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/QEMU_CODE.fd bs=1M count=64
            dd if=Build/ArmVirtQemu-AArch64/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/QEMU_EFI.fd of=Build/ArmVirtQemu-AArch64/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/QEMU_CODE.fd conv=notrunc
            dd if=/dev/zero of=Build/ArmVirtQemu-AArch64/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/QEMU_VARS.fd bs=1M count=64
        ;;

        RISCV64)
            # Does not yet appear to support secure boot
            echo "Building RiscVVirtPkg ($_ARCH)"
            _build_options=(
                -p OvmfPkg/RiscVVirt/RiscVVirtQemu.dsc
                -a "$_ARCH"
                "${_CC_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_EFI_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_NETWORK_TLS[@]}"
            )
            BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build "${_build_options[@]}"
            # Create tmp files so we don't overwrite things
            dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=32 | tee Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd.tmp Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd.tmp
            dd if=Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd of=Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd.tmp conv=notrunc
            dd if=Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd of=Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd.tmp conv=notrunc
            mv -v Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd{.tmp,}
            mv -v Build/RiscVVirtQemu/RELEASE_CLANGDWARF/FV/RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd{.tmp,}
        ;;

        X64)
            echo "Building ovmf ($_ARCH) with microvm support (4MB FD)"
            _build_options=(
                -p OvmfPkg/Microvm/Microvm$_ARCH.dsc
                -a "$_ARCH"
                "${_CC_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_EFI_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_NETWORK_TLS[@]}"
            )
            BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build "${_build_options[@]}"
            mv -v Build/MicrovmX64{,-4mb}

            echo "Building ovmf ($_ARCH) with secure boot support (4MB FD)"
            _build_options=(
                -p OvmfPkg/OvmfPkgIa32X64.dsc
                -a IA32
                -a "${_ARCH}"
                "${_CC_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_EFI_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_NETWORK_TLS[@]}"
                -D SECURE_BOOT_ENABLE
                -D SMM_REQUIRE
            )
            BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build "${_build_options[@]}"
            mv -v Build/Ovmf3264{,-secure-4mb}

            echo "Building ovmf (${_ARCH}) without secure boot (4MB FD)"
            _build_options=(
                -p OvmfPkg/OvmfPkg$_ARCH.dsc
                -a "$_ARCH"
                "${_CC_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_EFI_OPTS[@]}"
                "${_NETWORK_TLS[@]}"
            )
            BaseTools/BinWrappers/PosixLike/build "${_build_options[@]}"
            mv -v Build/OvmfX64{,-4mb}
        ;;
    esac
done
packages.install:
# QEMU descriptors

packages.install:
if [ -d ../compat ]; then
    pushd ../compat
    %make_install

    # Version libs
    pushd %(installroot)
    f=""
    for f in usr/lib/ffmpeg-8.1/*; do
        if [[ $f == *.so ]]; then
            ln -srf -- usr/lib/"$(readlink "$f")" "$f"
            mv "$f" "${f%%.so}-8.1.so"
        elif [[ ! -d $f ]]; then
            mv "$f" usr/lib
        fi
    done

    # Rename pkgconfigs so they don't conflict
    mv %(installroot)%(libdir)/ffmpeg-8.1/pkgconfig %(installroot)%(libdir)/pkgconfig
    cd %(installroot)%(libdir)/pkgconfig
    for i in *.pc; do
        mv $i ${i%.pc}-8.1.pc
    done

    # Fixup pkgconfig dependencies
    for b in avcodec avdevice avfilter avformat avutil postproc swresample swscale; do
        sed -i "s|lib$b|lib$b-8.1|g" *.pc
        sed -i "s|-l$b|-l$b-8.1|g" *.pc
    done
    popd

    # Delete everything unversioned
    rm -rfv %(installroot)%(bindir)/ \
            %(installroot)%(datadir)/ffmpeg \
            %(installroot)%(docdir) \
            %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1 \
            %(installroot)%(mandir)/man3
    rmdir -v %(installroot)%(mandir) \
            %(installroot)%(datadir)
    popd
fi

%make_install

# Deprecated lib(s)
for i in libpostproc{,-devel}; do
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(docdir)/${i}
    echo "DEPRECATED" > %(installroot)%(docdir)/${i}/README

    # PGO

    env \
        JARLOG_FILE="${PWD}/jarlog" \

        MOZ_REMOTE_SETTINGS_DEVTOOLS=1 \

    dbus-run-session \
        wlheadless-run \
            -c weston --width=1920 --height=1080 \
            -- ./mach python build/pgo/profileserver.py

    # Make sure PGO data is present
    stat -c "Profile data found (%%s bytes)" merged.profdata
    test -s merged.profdata
    stat -c "Jar log found (%%s bytes)" jarlog
    test -s jarlog

    # Delete instrumented browser
    ./mach clobber objdir

    # Reset mozconfig
    cp mozconfig.save mozconfig

    # Enable LTO
    echo "ac_add_options MOZ_LTO=cross,full" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-lto=cross,full" >> mozconfig

    # PGO
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-profile-use=cross" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --with-pgo-profile-path=${PWD}/merged.profdata" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --with-pgo-jarlog=${PWD}/jarlog" >> mozconfig

    ./mach build

%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/0001-Downstream-Don-t-run-fixincludes-during-install.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/disable-rpath.patch

function gcc_configure() {
    ../configure \
        --build=%(host_platform) \
        --host=%(host_platform) \
        --prefix=/usr \
        --libdir=%(libdir) \
        --libexecdir=%(libdir) \
        --disable-libssp \
        --enable-cet \
        --enable-checking=release \
        --enable-default-pie \
        --enable-default-ssp \
        --enable-gnu-indirect-function \
        --enable-host-bind-now \
        --enable-host-pie \
        --enable-link-serialization \
        --enable-linker-build-id \
        --enable-multilib \
        --enable-plugin \
        --enable-shared \
        --enable-threads=yes \
        --with-arch=%(march) \
        --with-arch_32=%(march) \
        --with-bugurl='https://github.com/AerynOS/recipes/issues' \
        --with-build-config=${_build_config} \
        --with-gcc-major-version-only \
        --with-gxx-libcxx-include-dir=/usr/include/c++/v1 \
        --with-isl \
        --with-linker-hash-style=gnu \
        --with-multilib-list=m32,m64 \
        --with-pkgversion="AerynOS" \
        --with-system-zlib \
        --with-tune=%(mtune) \
        --with-tune_32=%(mtune) \
        "$@"
}

mkdir gcc_build libgccjit_build

pushd gcc_build
gcc_configure \
    --enable-bootstrap \
    --enable-languages=c,c++,cobol,fortran,rust
popd

# Build libgccjit separately to avoid building all compilers with enable-host-shared which has a performance penalty
# I didn't test that but both Arch and Fedora has the same note in their repos
# TODO: Test that
pushd libgccjit_build
gcc_configure \
    --disable-bootstrap \
    --enable-host-shared \
    --enable-languages=jit \
    --enable-libgdiagnostics
popd
packages.install:
%make_install -C gcc_build

# libgccjit
DESTDIR="%(installroot)" %make -C gcc_build/gcc jit.install-common jit.install-info

# libgdiagnostics
DESTDIR="%(installroot)" %make -C libgccjit_build/gcc install-libgdiagnostics

# Info files
for lib in libgomp libitm libquadmath; do
    DESTDIR="%(installroot)" %make -C gcc_build/%(host_platform)/${lib} install-info
done

# bfd needs to be able to find the LTO plugin
major_version=$(echo %(version) | cut -d. -f1)
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(libdir)/bfd-plugins
ln -srfv %(installroot)/%(libdir)/gcc/%(build_platform)/${major_version}/liblto_plugin.so %(installroot)/%(libdir)/bfd-plugins/liblto_plugin.so

# gdb needs to autoload some files, maybe lldb piggy backs off this?
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/gdb/auto-load/%(libdir)
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/gdb/auto-load/%(libdir)32
mv %(installroot)/%(libdir)/libstdc++.so.*-gdb.py %(installroot)/%(datadir)/gdb/auto-load/%(libdir)/.
mv %(installroot)/%(libdir)32/libstdc++.so.*-gdb.py %(installroot)/%(datadir)/gdb/auto-load/%(libdir)32/.
%python_compile

# Causes file conflicts
rm -rv %(installroot)%(datadir)/info/dir

# Clang provides c++ on Aeryn
rm -v %(installroot)%(bindir)/c++ %(installroot)%(bindir)/%(host_platform)-c++

# Make x86_64-solus-linux a target alias of x86_64-aerynos-linux, and add compat targets for common x86 targets
pushd %(installroot)/%(bindir)
for compat in x86_64-solus-linux x86_64-linux-gnu x86_64-pc-linux-gnu; do
    for i in g++ gcc gcc-${major_version} gcc-ar gcc-nm gcc-ranlib gccrs gfortran ; do
        ln -sv %(host_platform)-${i} ${compat}-${i}
    done
    ln -srv %(installroot)/usr/include/c++/${major_version}/%(host_platform) %(installroot)/usr/include/c++/${major_version}/${compat}
    ln -srv %(installroot)/usr/lib/gcc/%(host_platform) %(installroot)/usr/lib/gcc/${compat}
done
popd

# TODO: Remove once we can remove gcc-devel and gcc-32bit-devel from the index
mkdir -p %(installroot)/usr/share/doc/replace/
touch %(installroot)/usr/share/doc/replace/gcc{,-32bit}-devel %(installroot)/usr/share/doc/replace/g++-32bit
touch %(installroot)/usr/share/doc/replace/libatomic{,-32bit}-static

# This is useful when updating to a new version or rebootstrapping the GCC toolchain

_build_step="profiledbootstrap"

packages.setup:
%patch %(pkgdir)/perf/0001-Remove-RELR-dependency-check.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/0001-sysdeps-Add-support-for-default-directories.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/0001-Force-correct-RTLDLIST-for-ldd.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/0001-Compress-charmaps-with-zstd.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/aerynos/0001-downstream-Update-default-PATH.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless/make-hosts-file-stateless.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless/Support-fallback-stateless-shells-path.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless/Use-a-stateless-ld.so.conf.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless/0001-Stateless-nsswitch.conf.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/stateless/ld-so-cache-in-var.patch

mkdir build && cd build
echo "LD_SO_CACHE=/var/cache/ldconfig/ld.so.cache" >> configparms
echo "slibdir=%(libdir)" >> configparms
echo "rtlddir=%(libdir)" >> configparms
echo "sbindir=%(sbindir)" >> configparms
echo "rootsbindir=%(sbindir)" >> configparms
# Note this deliberately excludes libsuffix and is not an error
echo "complocaledir=/usr/lib/locale" >> configparms

# CET is strict (cet_elf_property): IBT/SHSTK are enabled for modules that
# advertise them, and dlopen() of a non-CET library fails while SHSTK is
# active. All our 64-bit packages are built with -fcf-protection; the 32-bit
# profile stays --disable-cet.
# SFrame is only supported on x86_64/aarch64 (not the 32-bit target)
../configure \
    $COMMON_GLIBC_OPTIONS \
    --enable-cet \
    --enable-sframe
packages.install:
%make_install build DESTDIR="%(installroot)" -C build

# Make gconv cache
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=%(installroot)/%(libdir) %(installroot)/%(libdir)/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 %(installroot)/usr/sbin/iconvconfig --prefix=%(installroot)

%make localedata/install-locale-files DESTDIR="%(installroot)" -C build

# We don't support nss_db/hesiod currently
rm -v %(installroot)/%(bindir)/makedb \
      %(installroot)/%(libdir)/libnss_db.so* \
      %(installroot)/%(libdir)/libnss_hesiod.so* \
      %(installroot)/var/db/Makefile
rmdir -v %(installroot)/var/db %(installroot)/var

# Stateless: Remove obsolete rpc
rm -v %(installroot)/etc/rpc
rmdir -v %(installroot)/etc

%install_file %(pkgdir)/ld.so.conf  %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/ld.so.conf
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/ld.so.conf.d

%install_file %(pkgdir)/glibc_ldconfig.yaml %(installroot)/usr/share/moss/triggers/sys.d/glibc_ldconfig.yaml


# Stateless: We need these directories to exist without including them
%tmpfiles "# Create stateless directories"
%tmpfiles "d /etc/ld.so.conf.d 0755 - - -"
%tmpfiles "d /var/cache/ldconfig 0755 - - -"
%tmpfiles "d /var/db 0755 - - -"
packages.environment:
# --enable-kernel tracks the fourth-most-recent LTS kernel (kernel.org longterm)

echo "rtlddir=%(libdir)" >> configparms

packages.name: gnome-keyring
packages.summary: gnome-keyring is a program that keep password and other secrets for users
packages.description:
gnome-keyring is a program that keep password and other secrets for users. It is run as a daemon in the session, similar to ssh-agent, and other applications locate it via an environment variable or a D-Bus.

The program can manage several keyrings, each with its own master password, and there is also a session keyring which is never stored to disk, but forgotten when the session ends.

The library libsecret is used by applications to integrate with the GNOME keyring system.

packages.name: gnu-coreutils-compat
packages.description:
The GNU Core Utilities are the basic file, shell and text manipulation utilities of the GNU operating system. These are the core utilities which are expected to exist on every operating system.

This package provides GNU versions of coreutils programs where the uutils implementation is known to be deficient relative to the GNU version in some way.
packages.setup:
export FORCE_UNSAFE_CONFIGURE=1
# There HAS to be a better way to do this
%configure \
    --enable-install-program=cp,mv,rm,rmdir,sort,stty \
    --enable-no-install-program=[,b2sum,base32,base64,basename,basenc,cat,chcon,chgrp,chmod,chown,chroot,cksum,comm,csplit,cut,date,dd,df,dir,dircolors,dirname,du,echo,env,expand,expr,factor,false,fmt,fold,groups,head,hostid,id,install,join,kill,link,ln,logname,ls,md5sum,mkdir,mkfifo,mknod,mktemp,nice,nl,nohup,nproc,numfmt,od,paste,pathchk,pinky,pr,printenv,printf,ptx,pwd,readlink,realpath,runcon,seq,sha1sum,sha224sum,sha256sum,sha384sum,sha512sum,shred,shuf,sleep,split,stat,stdbuf,sum,sync,tac,tail,tee,test,timeout,touch,tr,true,truncate,tsort,tty,uname,unexpand,uniq,unlink,uptime,users,vdir,wc,who,whoami,yes,
packages.install:
%make_install

# Why isn't this removed by the above list?
rm -v %(installroot)/%(bindir)/install \
      %(installroot)/%(mandir)/man1/install.1

# Rename so gnu coreutils tools don't conflict with uutils coreutils tools
cd %(installroot)/%(bindir)
for i in *; do
    mv -v ${i} gnu-${i}
done

cd %(installroot)/%(mandir)/man1/
for i in *; do
    mv -v ${i} gnu-${i}
done

    -j%(jobs)

    platform=linuxbsd
    use_llvm=yes

    debug_symbols=no

    use_sowrap=false # Don't use dlopen()

    vulkan=true
    use_volk=false # Not needed when linking to libvulkan
    wayland=true
    x11=false

    builtin_brotli=false
    builtin_certs=false
    builtin_freetype=false
    builtin_glslang=false
    builtin_graphite=false
    builtin_libogg=false
    builtin_libpng=false
    builtin_libwebp=false
    builtin_pcre2=false
    builtin_zlib=false
    builtin_zstd=false
)

%ccache_zero
scons "${_scons_args[@]}"
%ccache_stats

packages.name: golang
packages.description: Go is an open source programming language that makes it easy to build simple, reliable, and efficient software.
packages.install:
%install_dir %(installroot)/${_goroot} %(installroot)/%(bindir)
cp -apv api bin doc lib pkg src misc test go.env VERSION %(installroot)/${_goroot}

# Fix group/all permissions
chmod -Rc g+rX,o+rX %(installroot)/${_goroot}/

# gdbinit file
%install_file %(pkgdir)/golang-gdbinit %(installroot)/usr/share/gdb/system-gdbinit/golang.gdb

# Symlinks are required so that golang can resolve the goroot at runtime
ln -srv %(installroot)/${_goroot}/bin/gofmt %(installroot)/%(bindir)/gofmt
ln -srv %(installroot)/${_goroot}/bin/go %(installroot)/%(bindir)/go

# Useless
rm -v %(installroot)/${_goroot}/src/go/doc/Makefile

# This is just data fed into tests, but boulder scans it regardless.
find %(installroot)/%(libdir) -type d -name testdata -exec rm -rfv {} +
packages.environment:
# This can mess up the automatic goroot detection if set. Explicitly unset it just in case it has made it's way into the buildenv
unset GOROOT

# Final goroot
_goroot="%(libdir)/%(name)"

# needed for bootstrap in the build phase
export GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP="${_goroot}"

# Set the CPU baseline to v2, which corresponds to x86_64v2
# Note, this is also propagated into the default build config for the distribution. ALL linux AMD64 binaries built with this golang distribution will default to v2
export GOAMD64=v2

packages.description:
Heaptrack traces all memory allocations and annotates these events with stack traces.
Dedicated analysis tools then allow you to interpret the heap memory profile to:

- find hotspots that need to be optimized to reduce the memory footprint of your application
- find memory leaks, i.e. locations that allocate memory which is never deallocated
- find allocation hotspots, i.e. code locations that trigger a lot of memory allocation calls
- find temporary allocations, which are allocations that are directly followed by their deallocation

Microcode package for Intel CPUs. You do not need to install this package unless
you are building a custom kernel for AerynOS, as the early boot code is built into
the kernel initrd images.
packages.install:
%install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/intel-ucode
%install_file intel-ucode-with-caveats/* %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/intel-ucode/.
%install_file intel-ucode/* %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/intel-ucode/.

# Construct early microcode initrd
%install_dir initrd/kernel/x86/microcode/
pushd initrd

touch kernel/x86/microcode/GenuineIntel.bin
for i in %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/intel-ucode/*; do
    cat ${i} >> kernel/x86/microcode/GenuineIntel.bin
done

find . -exec touch -d @0 {} \;
find . | cpio -o -H newc --device-independent --reproducible > ../intel-microcode.initrd
popd
%install_file intel-microcode.initrd %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/initrd.d/00-intel-microcode.initrd

for file in license releasenote.md README.md; do
    %install_file $file %(installroot)%(docdir)/intel-microcode/$file
done

function libarchive_configure() {
    %patch %(pkgdir)/0001-Add-stone-read-support.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/0001-Exclude-boulder-broken-test.patch

    %reconfigure \
        --disable-rpath \
        --with-lzo2 \
        --with-libstone \
        "$@"
}

pushd libarchive
    libarchive_configure \
        --disable-static \
        --enable-shared
popd

# Statically link in libxml2 and libicu since those are the libraries most likely to change sonames
# libstone doesn't yet have a stable ABI and it's not needed so don't bother supporting it here.
pushd libarchive-static
    libarchive_configure \
        --enable-bsdcpio=static \
        --enable-static \
        --disable-bsdcat \
        --disable-bsdcpio \
        --disable-bsdunzip \
        --disable-shared \
        --without-libstone \
        LIBXML2_PC_LIBS="$(pkg-config --variable=libdir libxml-2.0)/libxml2.a $(pkg-config --variable=libdir icu-uc)/libicuuc.a $(pkg-config --variable=libdir icu-uc)/libicudata.a -lstdc++ -lm" \
        ac_cv_lib_xml2_xmlInitParser=yes
popd
packages.build:
for i in libarchive-static libarchive; do
    cat ${i}/Makefile
    %ccache_zero
    env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/${i}" %make -C ${i} V=1
    %ccache_stats
done

%make_install -C libarchive-static

packages.name: libostree
packages.summary: Operating system and container binary deployment and upgrades
packages.description:
The core OSTree model is like git in that it checksums individual files and has a content-addressed-object store. It's unlike git in that it "checks out" the files via hardlinks, and they thus need to be immutable to prevent corruption. Therefore, another way to think of OSTree is that it's just a more polished version of Linux VServer hardlinks.

Features:
- Transactional upgrades and rollback for the system
- Replicating content incrementally over HTTP via GPG signatures and “pinned TLS” support
- Support for parallel installing more than just 2 bootable roots
- Binary history on the server side (and client)
- Introspectable shared library API for build and deployment systems
- Flexible support for multiple branches and repositories, supporting projects like Flatpak which use libostree for applications, rather than hosts.
packages.install:
%make_install
# we're not an ostree distribution
rm -rf %(installroot)%(libdir)/systemd/
rm -rf %(installroot)%(libdir)/tmpfiles.d

# We don't support grub
rm -rfv %(installroot)%(libdir)/libostree/libostree/grub2-15_ostree
rmdir -v %(installroot)%(libdir)/libostree/libostree/ \
         %(installroot)%(libdir)/libostree/

packages.name: libtsm
packages.description:
TSM is a state machine for DEC VT100-VT520 compatible terminal emulators. It tries to support all common standards while keeping compatibility to existing emulators like xterm, gnome-terminal, konsole, ..

TSM itself does not provide any rendering nor window management. It is a simple plain state machine without any external dependencies. It can be used to implement terminal emulators, but also to implement other applications that      need to interpret terminal escape sequences.

This library is very similar to libvte of the gnome project. However, libvte is highly bound to GTK+, which makes it unsuitable for non-graphics projects that need to parse escape sequences. Instead, TSM tries to restrict its API      to terminal emulation only. Furthermore, TSM does not try to establish a new terminal emulation standard, but instead keeps compatibility as close to xterm as possible. This is why the TERM variable can be set to xterm-color256      with any TSM based terminal emulator.

packages.name: libxcb
packages.summary: C interface to the X Window System protocol, which replaces the traditional Xlib interface.
packages.description:
libxcb provides an interface to the X Window System protocol, which
replaces the traditional Xlib interface. It has several advantages over
Xlib, including:

- size: small, simple library, and lower memory footprint
- latency hiding: batch several requests and wait for the replies later
- direct protocol access: interface and protocol correspond exactly
- proven thread support: transparently access XCB from multiple threads
  easy extension implementation: interfaces auto-generated from XML-XCB

Xlib also uses XCB as a transport layer, allowing software to make
requests and receive responses with both, which eases porting to XCB.
However, client programs, libraries, and toolkits will gain the most
benefit from a native XCB port.

packages.name: libxcrypt
packages.description:
libxcrypt is a modern library for one-way hashing of passwords. It supports a wide variety of both modern and historical hashing methods: yescrypt, gost-yescrypt, scrypt, bcrypt, sha512crypt, sha256crypt, md5crypt, SunMD5, sha1crypt, NT, bsdicrypt, bigcrypt, and descrypt. It provides the traditional Unix crypt and crypt_r interfaces, as well as a set of extended interfaces pioneered by Openwall Linux, crypt_rn, crypt_ra, crypt_gensalt, crypt_gensalt_rn, and crypt_gensalt_ra.
libxcrypt is intended to be used by login(1), passwd(1), and other similar programs; that is, to hash a small number of passwords during an interactive authentication dialogue with a human. It is not suitable for use in bulk password-cracking applications, or in any other situation where speed is more important than careful handling of sensitive data. However, it is intended to be fast and lightweight enough for use in servers that must field thousands of login attempts per minute.

packages.setup:

    5a3f625f2e9d9f70134af2340d82af3f19ae6891
    585d96e825a5eb8a3e406c054059e3bfeb0e963f
)
_reverts=(
)
for c in "${_backports[@]}"; do
    echo Backporting $(git log --oneline -1 "${c}")
    git cherry-pick -n "${c}"
done
for c in "${_reverts[@]}"; do
    echo Reverting $(git log --oneline -1 "${c}")
    git revert -n "${c}"
done
packages.install:
make install-zst FIRMWAREDIR=/usr/lib/firmware DESTDIR=%(installroot)

# Remove conflicting and/or forbidden assets
for forbidden in carl9170fw qed Makefile GPL-3 ; do
    rm -rvf "%(installroot)/%(libdir)/firmware/${forbidden}"
done

# Construct early microcode initrd
%install_dir initrd/kernel/x86/microcode/
pushd initrd

touch kernel/x86/microcode/AuthenticAMD.bin
for i in %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/amd-ucode/*.bin; do
    cat ${i} >> kernel/x86/microcode/AuthenticAMD.bin
done
find . -exec touch -d @0 {} \;
find . | cpio -o -H newc --device-independent --reproducible > ../amd64-microcode.initrd
popd
%install_file amd64-microcode.initrd %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/initrd.d/00-amd64-microcode.initrd

# Construct initrd for PSP firmware files (the only known kernel module in the initrd that requires firmware)
# Note that this includes a few unnecessary firmware files. Redo this once we can scan the modules for what they need directly
%install_dir initrdpsp/%(libdir)/firmware/amd/

for i in %(installroot)%(libdir)/firmware/amd/*.sbin.zst; do
    cp ${i} initrdpsp/%(libdir)/firmware/amd/
done
for i in initrdpsp/%(libdir)/firmware/amd/*.sbin.zst; do
    unzstd --rm ${i}
done

pushd initrdpsp
find . -exec touch -d @0 {} \;

# Copy headers and essential directories
for i in include scripts Documentation ; do
    cp -R ${i} ${dstDir}/
done

# Copy architecture specific headers
(find arch -name include -type d -print | xargs -n1 -i: find : -type f) | cpio -pd --preserve-modification-time ${dstDir}

# Media driver headers
for dir in "drivers/media/dvb-frontends" "drivers/media/tuners"; do
    find ${dir} -name "*.h" -exec cp --parents {} ${dstDir} \;
done
find drivers/media/platform -name "*.h" -exec cp --parents {} ${dstDir} \;

# Clean unnecessary files
find ${dstDir}/scripts -name "*.o" -delete

# Copy build requirements
for i in Module.symvers System.map .config ; do
    %install_file ${i} ${dstDir}/
done
%install_exe tools/objtool/objtool ${dstDir}/tools/objtool/objtool
chmod 00755 ${dstDir}/scripts/basic/fixdep

# Set up module symlinks
rm -vf %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${kernelVersion}/build || :
rm -vf %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${kernelVersion}/source || :
ln -svf build %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${kernelVersion}/source
ln -svf ${headersDir} %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${kernelVersion}/build

# Compress modules with zstd
find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

################################################################################
#
# linux-headers below this block.
#
# If you are copying this recipe for a variant kernel (linux-lts/linux-gaming)
#  DO NOT include anything below this.
#
################################################################################

# linux-headers
%make ${_common_make_build_args} INSTALL_HDR_PATH=%(installroot)%(prefix) headers_install

# Ensure that amdgpu HDMI 2.1 Fixed Rate Link (FRL) support in the open-source AMDGPU display driver gets enabled.
# AMD initially keeps FRL disabled by default, until Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) code is fully integrated.
%install_file %(pkgdir)/20-linux-stable-amdgpu-feature-mask-vrr.cmdline -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/kernel/cmdline.d/

function apply_llvm_patches() {

    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-PATCH-clang-Don-t-install-static-libraries.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-downstream-Suppress-runpath-in-openmp.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-bolt-Set-version-string.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-openmp-Don-t-install-static-libarcher.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-polly-Create-targets-for-headers-cmake.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-offload-Fix-build-failure-with-icf-all.patch

    # our build system
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-Make-gnuhash-the-default-when-not-specified.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-lld-Use-zstd-compression-for-debug-symbols-by-defaul.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-lld-Always-enable-build-id-and-use-20-byte-hashes.patch

    # Aeryn-specific patches
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Support-aeryn-solus-as-a-distro.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Use-correct-Serpent-OS-multilib-paths-for-ld.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Update-binutils-version-to-match-Serpent-OS.patch

    # Performance-related patches
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/perf/0001-Use-mimalloc-for-clang-lld-llvm.patch

    ## Upstream backports/reverts

    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0001-BOLT-X86-Add-missing-MOV8-instruction-cases-in-X86MC.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/bolt-fix-relr-addends-for-non-zero-image.patch

    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/219861.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/add-option-merge-text-sections.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/avoid-large-caps-in-dso-layout.patch
}

# "Inspired by"/"Gratuitously copied from" Gentoo, use LLVM_DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENTS to avoid installing static libs
# and other unnecessary things. This works by extracting the target list from ninja and
# filtering it to only have the things we really need. This way when cmake target files
# are generated it results in the components we didn't include not being added to the
# searched for objects.
## NOTE: New versions of LLVM should be built without this in order to see what's been
## added/removed and this list updated correspondingly.
function get_distribution_components() {
    # This generates a lot of output that we don't need to see
    set +x
    local target
    ninja -C "%(builddir)" -t targets | grep -Po 'install-\K.*(?=-stripped:)' | while read -r target; do
        case $target in
            distribution)
                continue
                ;;

            ### LLVM
            llvm-libraries)
                continue
                ;;
            # shared libraries
            LLVM|LLVMgold|LTO|Remarks)
                ;;
            # Used by LDC
            LLVMTableGen|LLVMSupport|LLVMDemangle)
                ;;
            # Devel
            llvm-headers|cmake-exports)
                ;;
            # Bins
            FileCheck|UnicodeNameMappingGenerator|dsymutil|llc|lli|llubi|obj2yaml|opt|opt-viewer|reduce-chunk-list|sancov|sanstats|split-file|verify-uselistorder|yaml2obj)
                ;;
            # Devel bins
            count|lli-child-target|not|yaml-bench)
                ;;
            # Test tools
            llvm-gpu-loader)
                continue
                ;;
            # Various binaries (everything we don't want has already been excluded)
            llvm-*)
                ;;

            ### Clang
            clang-libraries)
                continue
                ;;
            clang-tidy-headers)
                continue
                ;;
            # Libs
            libclang|clang-cpp)
                ;;
            clang|clangd|clang-*|bash-autocomplete)
                ;;
            # Other clang tools
            c-index-test|diagtool|find-all-symbols|hmaptool|modularize|offload-arch|pp-trace|scan-view|scan-build*)
                ;;
            clang*|findAllSymbols)
                continue
                ;;

            ### LLD
            # Shared libraries
            lld|lld-libraries)
                ;;
            # Devel
            lld-headers|lld-cmake-exports)
                ;;

            ### LLDB
            # bin
            lldb|lldb-python-scripts|lldb-argdumper|lldb-dap|lldb-instr|lldb-mcp|lldb-server)
                ;;
            # libs
            liblldb|lldbIntelFeatures)
                ;;
            # Devel
            lldb-headers)
                ;;

            ### Polly
            # Libs
            Polly|PollyISL|LLVMPolly)
                ;;
            # Devel
            polly-headers|polly-cmake-exports)
                ;;

            ### BOLT
            bolt)
                ;;

            ### MLIR
            mlir-libraries)
                continue
                ;;
            # Shared libs
            MLIR|MLIR-C|MLIRExecutionEngineShared)
                ;;
            # Target libs
            mlir_*)
                ;;
            # MLIR tools
            mlir-*|tblgen-lsp-server|tblgen-to-irdl)
                ;;
            # Devel
            mlir-headers|mlir-cmake-exports)
                ;;
            # MLIR dependencies
            MLIRSparseTensorRuntime|MLIRSparseTensorEnums)
                ;;

            ### Flang
            # Flang itself
            flang)
                ;;
            # Supporting tools
            bbc|tco|f18-parse-demo|fir-*)
                ;;
            # Fortran build files
            flang-binding|flang-module-interfaces|flang-fortran-binding)
                ;;

            ### built-ins, Runtimes
            builtins|runtimes)
                ;;

            ### Deny everything else
            *)
                continue
                ;;
        esac
        echo $target
    done
    set -x
}

emul32.setup:
apply_llvm_patches

cmake_llvm_configure -S llvm \
    -DLLVM_USE_LINKER="lld"

distribution_components=$(get_distribution_components | paste -sd\;)
test -n "$distribution_components"
cmake_llvm_configure -S llvm \
    -DLLVM_USE_LINKER="lld" \
    -DLLVM_DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENTS="$distribution_components"
emul32.install:
DESTDIR="%(installroot)" cmake --build "%(builddir)" --verbose --target install-distribution

### LLVM (begin)
# Force this to 32-bit specific configuration
mv %(installroot)%(bindir)/llvm-config %(installroot)%(bindir)/llvm-config32
ln -srv %(installroot)%(bindir)/llvm-config32 %(installroot)%(bindir)/llvm-config32-${_MAJOR_VERSION}
mv %(installroot)%(includedir)/llvm/Config/llvm-config.h %(installroot)%(includedir)/llvm/Config/llvm-config32.h

# Make sure that the .defs files are arch-dependent
mkdir %(installroot)/usr/include/llvm/Config/32
mv %(installroot)/usr/include/llvm/Config/*.def %(installroot)/usr/include/llvm/Config/32/
# LLVM (end)

### libcxx/libunwind (begin)
# Origin: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kraj/meta-clang/master/recipes-devtools/clang/clang/libunwind.pc.in
%install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/pkgconfig
sed -e 's@\@LIBDIR\@@%(libdir)@g' -e 's/@VERSION@/%(version)/g' %(pkgdir)/libunwind.pc.in > %(installroot)%(libdir)/pkgconfig/libunwind.pc
# libcxx/libunwind (end)

    install-docs-lldb-man \
    install-docs-llvm-dwarfdump-man \
    install-docs-llvm-man \

       %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/lldb-tblgen*

    export PATH="%(installroot)/usr/bin:${PATH}"
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="%(installroot)/%(libdir)"

    export BOLTED_BINS="/usr/lib/libclang-cpp.so.${_MAJOR_VERSION}.1 /usr/lib/libLLVM.so.${_MAJOR_VERSION}.1"

    for i in ${BOLTED_BINS}; do
      %bolt_instr %(installroot)/$i
    done

    cmake -G Ninja -B bolt-clang -S runtimes \
      -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="%(installroot)/usr/bin/clang" \
      -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="%(installroot)/usr/bin/clang++" \
      -DLLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES='libcxx;libcxxabi;libunwind' \
      -DLLVM_USE_LINKER="%(installroot)/usr/bin/ld.lld" \
      -DLLVM_ENABLE_LTO=Full
    ninja -C bolt-clang

%install_file %(pkgdir)/llvm-config.h %(installroot)%(includedir)/llvm/Config/llvm-config.h

# "Inspired by"/"Gratuitously copied from" Gentoo, use LLVM_DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENTS to avoid installing static libs
# and other unnecessary things. This works by extracting the target list from ninja and
# filtering it to only have the things we really need. This way when cmake target files
# are generated it results in the components we didn't include not being added to the
# searched for objects.
## NOTE: New versions of LLVM should be built without this in order to see what's been
## added/removed and this list updated correspondingly.
function get_distribution_components() {
    # This generates a lot of output that we don't need to see
    set +x
    local target
    ninja -C "%(builddir)" -t targets | grep -Po 'install-\K.*(?=-stripped:)' | while read -r target; do
        case $target in
            distribution)
                continue
                ;;

            ### LLVM
            llvm-libraries)
                continue
                ;;
            # shared libraries
            LLVM|LLVMgold|LTO|Remarks)
                ;;
            # Used by LDC
            LLVMTableGen|LLVMSupport|LLVMDemangle|LLVMDebuginfod)
                ;;
            # Devel
            llvm-headers|cmake-exports)
                ;;
            # Bins
            FileCheck|UnicodeNameMappingGenerator|bugpoint|dsymutil|llc|lli|obj2yaml|opt|opt-viewer|reduce-chunk-list|sancov|sanstats|split-file|verify-uselistorder|yaml2obj)
                ;;
            # Devel bins
            count|lli-child-target|not|yaml-bench)
                ;;
            # Various binaries (everything we don't want has already been excluded)
            llvm-*)
                ;;

            ### Clang
            clang-libraries)
                continue
                ;;
            clang-tidy-headers)
                continue
                ;;
            # Libs
            libclang|clang-cpp)
                ;;
            clang|clangd|clang-*|bash-autocomplete)
                ;;
            # Other clang tools
            amdgpu-arch|c-index-test|diagtool|find-all-symbols|hmaptool|modularize|nvptx-arch|pp-trace|scan-view|scan-build*)
                ;;
            clang*|findAllSymbols)
                continue
                ;;

            ### LLD
            # Shared libraries
            lld*)
                ;;
            # Devel
            lld-headers|lld-cmake-exports)
                ;;

            ### built-ins, Runtimes
            builtins|runtimes)
                ;;

            ### Deny everything else
            *)
                continue
                ;;
        esac
        echo $target
    done
    set -x
}

function apply_llvm_patches() {
    # Build-related patches, achieving adjustments/fixes to the build that cannot be done via cmake flags
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-Build-lld-libraries-shared.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-Build-polly-libraries-shared.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-PATCH-clang-Don-t-install-static-libraries.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-downstream-Suppress-runpath-in-openmp.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-bolt-Set-version-string.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-openmp-Don-t-install-static-libarcher.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-polly-Create-targets-for-headers-cmake.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-offload-Fix-build-failure-with-icf-all.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/build/0001-Emit-relocations-for-BOLT.patch

    # Runtime config changes. These often duplicate settings set by our CFLAGS/LDFLAGS and are intended as sane
    # defaults when a build either doesn't respect our flags or when a user is building a project outside of
    # our build system
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-Make-gnuhash-the-default-when-not-specified.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-lld-Use-zstd-compression-for-debug-symbols-by-defaul.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/config/0001-lld-Always-enable-build-id-and-use-20-byte-hashes.patch

    # Aeryn-specific patches
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Support-aeryn-solus-as-a-distro.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Use-correct-Serpent-OS-multilib-paths-for-ld.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/aerynos/0001-Update-binutils-version-to-match-Serpent-OS.patch

    # Performance-related patches
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/perf/0001-Use-mimalloc-for-clang-lld-llvm.patch

    ## Upstream backports/reverts
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0001-Backport-177953.patch
    # Fix ffmpeg build
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0001-SLP-Support-for-tree-throttling-in-SLP-graphs-with-g.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0002-X86-vectorizeExtractedCast-don-t-assume-vector-sourc.patch
    # Fixes rust 1.97 miscompilation
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/208683.patch
    # Fix rustc bpf support + prereq
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0001-bpf-Support-aggregate-returns-190894.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/patches/upstream/0002-Fixes-for-compile-rust-code-192134.patch
}

packages.description:
Mailspring is an email client forked from Nylas Mail and built with Electron.
Its sync engine (mailsync) is written in C++ and runs locally, storing mail in
a local SQLite database.
packages.setup:
%patch %(pkgdir)/0001-hicolor-icon.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/0002-disable-update-check.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-static-libstdcxx.patch

# node 24: pin yauzl to fix an extract-zip deadlock during `npm install`
node -e "const fs = require('fs'); \
    ['package.json', 'app/package.json'].forEach(f => { \
        const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f)); \
        pkg.overrides = pkg.overrides || {}; \
        pkg.overrides.yauzl = '^3.3.2'; \
        fs.writeFileSync(f, JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n'); \
    });"

# The mailsync submodule is checked out, so postinstall.js will not download
# a prebuilt binary and we build the engine ourselves in the build phase.
npm install
packages.build:
_deps="%(buildroot)/mailsync-deps"

# Build the vendored, Mailspring-patched libetpan that mailsync links
# statically. MailCore2 and mailsync both need it before they configure.
pushd mailsync/Vendor/libetpan
# autoconf 2.72 selects C23, where libetpan's old-style (K&R) function
# definitions no longer parse. Build it as C17.
export CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -std=gnu17"
%autogen
%make
%make install DESTDIR="${_deps}"
popd

export CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -I${_deps}/usr/include"
export CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS} -I${_deps}/usr/include"

# The engine's CMakeLists expects MailCore2's build tree at
# Vendor/mailcore2/build.
pushd mailsync/Vendor/mailcore2
cmake -G Ninja \
    -B build \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH="${_deps}/usr/include" \
    -DCMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH="${_deps}/usr/lib"
ninja -C build MailCore
popd

pushd mailsync
%cmake \
    -DCMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH="${_deps}/usr/include" \
    -DCMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH="${_deps}/usr/lib" \
    -DCMAKE_SKIP_RPATH=ON \
    -DETPAN_LIB="${_deps}/usr/lib/libetpan.a"
%cmake_build
popd

# electron-packager picks this up as resources/app.asar.unpacked/mailsync
cp mailsync/%(builddir)/mailsync app/mailsync

npm run build -- --skip-installers
packages.install:
mailspringdir=%(libdir)/%(name)

%install_dir %(installroot)$mailspringdir
cp -a app/dist/mailspring-linux-x64/* %(installroot)$mailspringdir

%install_dir %(installroot)%(bindir)
ln -srv %(installroot)$mailspringdir/mailspring %(installroot)%(bindir)/mailspring

for i in "Mailspring.desktop" "mailspring.metainfo.xml"; do
    sed -e "s|<%%= productName %%>|Mailspring|g" \
        -e "s|<%%= name %%>|mailspring|g" \
        -e "s|<%%= description %%>|The best email app for people and teams at work|g" \
        app/build/resources/linux/${i}.in > ./$i
done

%install_file Mailspring.desktop -t %(installroot)/usr/share/applications/
%install_file mailspring.metainfo.xml -t %(installroot)/usr/share/metainfo/

for i in 16 32 64 128 256 512; do
    %install_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/${i}x${i}/apps
    %install_file app/build/resources/linux/icons/${i}.png %(installroot)/%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/${i}x${i}/apps/mailspring.png

%patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-openssl-4-2.patch

# patch taken from Homebrew, adapted for nodejs-22
# https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/blob/master/Patches/node/icu4c-79.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-icu4c-79.patch

python configure.py \
    --ninja \
    --enable-lto \
    --prefix=%(prefix) \
    --libdir=lib \
    --shared \
    --shared-brotli \
    --shared-cares \
    --shared-libuv \
    --shared-nghttp2 \
    --shared-nghttp3 \
    --shared-ngtcp2 \
    --shared-openssl \
    --shared-sqlite \
    --shared-zlib \
    --shared-zstd \
    --verbose \
    --with-intl=system-icu
packages.install:
mv -v out/Release/lib/libnode.so.* out/Release/
./tools/install.py install --dest-dir %(installroot) --prefix %(prefix)

mv %(installroot)/%(libdir)/node_modules \
   %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB

# Fix the node permissions and move it
chmod 0755 %(installroot)/%(bindir)/node
patchelf --remove-rpath %(installroot)/%(bindir)/node
mv %(installroot)/%(bindir)/node %(installroot)/%(bindir)/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR


# Move the corepack binary
rm -f %(installroot)/%(bindir)/corepack

# Set the hashbang to use the matching Node.js interpreter
sed --in-place --regexp-extended \
    "s;^#!/usr/bin/env node($|\ |\t)+;#!/usr/bin/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR;g" \
    %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/corepack/dist/corepack.js

ln -srf %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/corepack/dist/corepack.js \
        %(installroot)/%(bindir)/corepack-$NODEJS_MAJOR


# Move the npm binary
rm -f %(installroot)/%(bindir)/npm

# Set the hashbang to use the matching Node.js interpreter
sed --in-place --regexp-extended \
    "s;^#!/usr/bin/env node($|\ |\t)+;#!/usr/bin/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR;g" \
    %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/bin/npm-cli.js

ln -srf %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/bin/npm-cli.js \
        %(installroot)/%(bindir)/npm-$NODEJS_MAJOR


# Move the npx binary
rm -f %(installroot)/%(bindir)/npx

# Set the hashbang to use the matching Node.js interpreter
sed --in-place --regexp-extended \
    "s;^#!/usr/bin/env node($|\ |\t)+;#!/usr/bin/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR;g" \
    %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/bin/npx-cli.js

ln -srf %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/bin/npx-cli.js \
        %(installroot)/%(bindir)/npx-$NODEJS_MAJOR


# We don't need docs
rm -rfv %(installroot)/usr/share/doc

mv %(installroot)/usr/share/man/man1/node.1 %(installroot)/usr/share/man/man1/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR.1

mv %(installroot)/usr/include/node %(installroot)/usr/include/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR

# Some NPM bundled deps are executable but should not be
find %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm \
    -not -path "%(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/bin/*" \
    -executable -type f \
    -exec chmod -x {} \;
# The above command is a little overzealous. Add a few permissions back.
chmod +x %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/run-script/lib/node-gyp-bin/node-gyp
chmod +x %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/node_modules/node-gyp/bin/node-gyp.js

# Fix node-gyp
sed --in-place --regexp-extended \
    "s;^#!/usr/bin/env node($|\ |\t)+;#!/usr/bin/node-$NODEJS_MAJOR;g" \
    %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/node_modules/node-gyp/bin/node-gyp.js

find %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/node_modules \( \
    -name '*.md'     -o \
    -name 'AUTHOR*'  -o \
    -name 'LICENSE*' -o \
    -name 'PULL*'    -o \
    -name Makefile   -o \
    -name appveyor.yml -o \
    -name doc  -o \
    -name docs -o \
    -name examples -o \
    -name 'license*' -o \
    -name '*.bak'  -o \
    -name '*.d.ts' -o \
    -name '*.markdown' -o \
    -name '.*.yml' -o \
    -name .editorconfig -o \
    -name .github -o \
    -name .nycrc \
    \) -exec rm -rfv {} +
rm -rfv %(installroot)/$NODEJS_PRIVATE_SITELIB/npm/docs

# Nothing links against this. If that ever becomes necessary we can re-add these with a customized pkgconfig
rm -rfv %(installroot)/%(includedir)

# This is a compat directory that is used when the binary name can't be overridden
# To use it do something like `export PATH=/usr/lib/nodejs-22/bin:$PATH`
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(libdir)/nodejs-$NODEJS_MAJOR/bin
for i in node npm npx corepack; do
    ln -srv %(installroot)/%(bindir)/$i-$NODEJS_MAJOR %(installroot)/%(libdir)/nodejs-$NODEJS_MAJOR/bin/$i
done

# This is a compat directory that is used when the binary name can't be overridden

%install_dir %(installroot)/%(libdir)/nodejs-$NODEJS_MAJOR/bin

packages.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make CC=${CC} LD=${LD} OBJCOPY=${OBJCOPY} KERNEL_UNAME=${_kernel} NV_VERBOSE=1 modules
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
packages.install:
# Various Nvidia modprobe settings (taken from CachyOS)
# https://github.com/CachyOS/CachyOS-Settings/blob/master/usr/lib/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf
%install_file %(pkgdir)/nvidia.modprobe %(installroot)%(libdir)/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf
# Sleep settings
# https://github.com/CachyOS/CachyOS-PKGBUILDS/blob/master/nvidia/nvidia-utils/nvidia-sleep.conf
%install_file %(pkgdir)/nvidia-sleep.modprobe %(installroot)%(libdir)/modprobe.d/nvidia-sleep.conf

%install_dir %(installroot)%(docdir)/%(name)/
echo "VIRTUAL" > %(installroot)%(docdir)/%(name)/README

# TODO: Eventually we want the modprobe configs in a separate initrd for deduplication

for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %install_file kernel-open/*.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/drivers/video

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
packages.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    tmp=${dir##*/}

    if [ "${tmp}" != "initrd.d" ]; then
        kernels+=(${tmp})
    fi
done

# TODO: Fix this just rejecting all LDFLAGS
unset LDFLAGS

# ccache needs to be enabled via conf option, not by setting the path

    extra_conf_opts="--enable-ccache"

    extra_conf_opts+=" --with-boot-jdk='%(workdir)/bootstrap-jdk'"
else
    extra_conf_opts+=" --with-boot-jdk='%(libdir)/openjdk-17'"
fi

# Git commit that corresponds to version
GITCOMMIT=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/openjdk/jdk17u.git refs/tags/jdk-%(version)-ga^{} | awk '{print $1}')
# Basically this finds the git tag with the same commit as the `version-ga` format and then
# parses it with regex to extract the -build part (so `17.0.17-ga` to match `17.0.17-10` and the output is `10`)
_version_build=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/openjdk/jdk17u.git | \
                        grep ${GITCOMMIT} | \
                        sed '/-ga^{}/d' | \
                        awk '{print $2}' | \
                        sed -nr "s/.*%(version)\+(.*)\^.*/\1/p")
echo "Version build detected as ${_version_build}"

chmod +x configure
%configure \
    --prefix="%(installroot)/usr" \
    --disable-warnings-as-errors \
    --disable-absolute-paths-in-output \
    --with-jvm-features=link-time-opt \
    --with-native-debug-symbols=internal \
    --with-stdc++lib=dynamic \
    --with-toolchain-type=clang \
    --with-version-build="${_version_build}" \
    --with-version-pre="" \
    --with-version-opt="aeryn" \
    --with-vendor-name=AerynOS \
    --with-vendor-url=https://AerynOS.com/ \
    --with-vendor-bug-url=https://github.com/AerynOS/recipes/issues \
    --with-vendor-vm-bug-url=https://github.com/AerynOS/recipes/issues \
    --with-freetype=system \
    --with-giflib=system \
    --with-harfbuzz=system \
    --with-lcms=system \
    --with-libjpeg=system \
    --with-libpng=system \
    --with-zlib=system \
    --with-extra-cflags="${CFLAGS}" \
    --with-extra-cxxflags="${CXXFLAGS}" \
    --with-extra-ldflags="${LDFLAGS}" \
    --with-jobs=%(jobs) \
    AR="${AR}" \
    NM="${NM}" \
    OBJCOPY="${OBJCOPY}" \
    OBJDUMP="llvm-objdump" \
    SORT="/usr/bin/gnu-sort" \
    STRIP="${STRIP}" \
    $extra_conf_opts
packages.install:
make install

jvm_dir="%(libdir)/%(name)"
%install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)
mv %(installroot)%(prefix)/jvm/openjdk-* %(installroot)${jvm_dir}
rmdir %(installroot)%(prefix)/jvm

# Use the system trust store instead of the bundled CA list
rm -f %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/lib/security/cacerts
ln -srv %(installroot)/etc/ssl/certs/java/cacerts %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/lib/security/cacerts

# Remove license files and demo files
rm -rfv %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/{legal,demo}/

# System headers
%install_dir %(installroot)%(includedir)
mv %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/include %(installroot)%(includedir)/%(name)
ln -srv %(installroot)%(includedir)/%(name) %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/include

# Man pages
%install_dir %(installroot)%(datadir)
mv %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/man %(installroot)%(datadir)
find %(installroot)%(mandir) -type f -print -exec rename -- ".1" "-17.1" {} \;

# System JVM symlinks for applications that check for this path
%install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/jvm
ln -srv %(installroot)${jvm_dir} %(installroot)%(libdir)/jvm/%(name)

# Fix binary symlinks
pushd %(installroot)%(bindir)
for bin in *; do
    rm -v ${bin}
    if test -f %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/bin/${bin}; then
        ln -srv %(installroot)${jvm_dir}/bin/${bin} ${bin}-17
    fi
done
popd

packages.name: playerctl
packages.description:
Playerctl is a command-line utility and library for controlling media players
that implement the MPRIS D-Bus Interface Specification. Playerctl makes it easy
to bind player actions, such as play and pause, to media keys. You can also get
metadata about the playing track such as the artist and title for integration
into statusline generators or other command-line tools.

For more advanced users, Playerctl provides an introspectable library available
in your favorite scripting language that allows more detailed control like the
ability to subscribe to media player events or get metadata such as artist and
title for the playing track.

Examples of players implementing the MPRIS D-Bus Interface Specification include
vlc, mpv, RhythmBox, web browsers, cmus, mpd, spotify and others.

# Everything below translated from Arch Linux PKGBUILD
%patch %(pkgdir)/set-flutter-paths.patch

# Use system SQLite instead of letting sqlite3.dart download a prebuilt libsqlite3.so from github
# during the build. The hook does not check HTTP status, so any github error page becomes a "hash
# mismatch" build failure. Write in the versioned lib since it checks unversioned by default
# https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/blob/main/sqlite3/doc/hook.md#system-provided-sqlite
%patch %(pkgdir)/use-system-sqlite.patch

flutter --disable-analytics
flutter pub get
packages.install:
_build_folder=build/linux/x64/release/bundle

# Not required at runtime as it's only used on Android
rm -fv ${_build_folder}/lib/libdartjni.so

%install_bin ${_build_folder}/%(name)

%install_dir %(installroot){%(datadir),%(libdir)}/%(name)
cp -a ${_build_folder}/data/* %(installroot)%(datadir)/%(name)/
cp -a ${_build_folder}/lib/* %(installroot)%(libdir)/%(name)/
chmod 0755 %(installroot)%(libdir)/%(name)/crashpad_handler

%install_file linux/packaging/com.edde746.%(name).desktop -t %(installroot)%(datadir)/applications/
%install_file assets/%(name).svg -t %(installroot)%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/
%install_file assets/%(name).png -t %(installroot)%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/1024x1024/apps/

# keep an rpath pointing at the bundled libs
patchelf --set-rpath "%(libdir)/%(name)" %(installroot)%(bindir)/%(name)
for lib in %(installroot)%(libdir)/%(name)/*.so; do
    patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN' "${lib}"
done

packages.setup:
# De-vendored and shipped externally
rm -v Lib/ensurepip/_bundled/pip-*-py3-none-any.whl

%patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-openssl-4.patch

# enable-experimental-jit apparently requires LLVM 19?
# enable-bolt has a very high (>64GB) memory requirement
%configure \
    --enable-experimental-jit=no \
    --enable-loadable-sqlite-extensions \
    --enable-optimizations \
    --enable-shared \
    --with-computed-gotos \
    --with-dbmliborder=gdbm \
    --with-lto \
    --with-platlibdir=lib%(libsuffix) \
    --with-ssl-default-suites=openssl \
    --with-system-expat \
    --with-system-libmpdec \
    --with-tail-call-interp \
    --with-wheel-pkg-dir=%(datadir)/python-wheels \
    --without-ensurepip
packages.install:
%make_install

# Python 3 is the default Python on AerynOS
ln -srvf %(installroot)/%(bindir)/python3 %(installroot)/%(bindir)/python
ln -srvf %(installroot)/%(bindir)/pydoc3 %(installroot)/%(bindir)/pydoc
ln -srvf %(installroot)/%(mandir)/man1/python3.1 %(installroot)/%(mandir)/man1/python.1

# Idle desktop and appdata
ln -srvf %(installroot)/%(bindir)/idle3 %(installroot)/%(bindir)/idle
%install_file %(pkgdir)/idle3.desktop -t %(installroot)/usr/share/applications/
%install_file %(pkgdir)/idle3.appdata.xml -t %(installroot)/usr/share/metainfo/
for i in 16 32 48 256; do
    %install_file Lib/idlelib/Icons/idle_${i}.png %(installroot)%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/${i}x${i}/apps/idle3.png
done

# Delete the Python test suite (this is only used for testing Python itself)
# If it's determined that this is actually needed it should be subpackaged
rm -rfv %(installroot)${_pylibdir}/test \
        %(installroot)${_pylibdir}/{ctypes,distutils,tkinter,lib2to3,unittest}/test{,s} \
        %(installroot)${_dynload_dir}/{_ctypes_test,_test,_xxtestfuzz}*.so

# Get rid of DOS batch files:
find %(installroot) -name \*.bat -print -exec rm {} \;

# Remove shebang lines from .py files that aren't executable, and
# remove executability from .py files that don't have a shebang line:
find %(installroot) -name \*.py \
    \( \( \! -perm /u+x,g+x,o+x -exec sed -e '/^#!/Q 0' -e 'Q 1' {} \; \
    -print -exec sed -i '1d' {} \; \) -o \( \
    -perm /u+x,g+x,o+x ! -exec grep -m 1 -q '^#!' {} \; \
    -exec chmod a-x {} \; \) \)

# Delete all existing pycache dirs before regenerating them
find %(installroot) -type d -name "__pycache__" -print -exec rm -rv {} + -depth

# Cleanup empty dirs
find %(installroot) -type d -empty -print -delete

# If bootstrapping a new version then it may be required to provide the old soname for a while just until rebuilds are complete
# This is obviously not ABI compatible but _boulder doesn't know that_
# cp %(installroot)%(libdir)/libpython3.14.so.1.0 %(installroot)%(libdir)/libpython3.11.so.1.0
# patchelf --set-soname libpython3.11.so.1.0 %(installroot)%(libdir)/libpython3.11.so.1.0

# Recompile pyc files
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="%(installroot)/${_dynload_dir}/:%(installroot)%(libdir)" \
    %(installroot)%(bindir)/python${_version_major_minor} -s -B -m compileall \
    -f -j %(jobs) -o 0 -o 1 -o 2 -s %(installroot) -p / %(installroot) --invalidation-mode=checked-hash \
    -x 'bad_coding|badsyntax'
