else
    rm -r setuptools/_vendor

    # Populate dependencies list for devendored deps
    sed '/^core =/,/]/!d' pyproject.toml > ../requirements.txt
    sed -i '1d;$d' ../requirements.txt
    sed -i '/^dependencies =/ {
        r ../requirements.txt
        s/^core =/dependencies =/
        }' pyproject.toml
fi
packages.build:
if [[ ${_bootstrap} == "1" ]]; then
    python -m bootstrap.build
else
    echo "Something to prevent bash syntax errors due to an empty if block"
    %pyproject_build
fi

if [[ ${_bootstrap} == "1" ]]; then
    python -m bootstrap.install dist/setuptools-*-py3-none-any.whl -d "%(installroot)"

    # Remove extra providers
    rm -rfv %(installroot)/usr/lib/python3.*/site-packages/setuptools/_vendor/*.dist-info/
else
    %pyproject_install

    # Delete vendored packages
    # TODO replace with python_version macro
    rm -rfv %(installroot)/%(libdir)/python3.*/site-packages/setuptools/_vendor/

    # Install wheel for virtualenv
    %install_file dist/*.whl -t %(installroot)%(datadir)/python-wheels
fi

find %(installroot) -type f -name "*.exe" -print -delete

packages.install:
%make_install

%install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/binfmt.d/
# Dash seems to mangle the formatting of the output binfmt files so use bash explicitly
bash ./scripts/qemu-binfmt-conf.sh \
    --systemd ALL \
    --exportdir "%(installroot)%(libdir)/binfmt.d/" \
    --qemu-path "%(bindir)" \
    --persistent yes \
    --preserve-argv0 yes

# Delete binfmt entries for any targets we don't support
find %(installroot)%(libdir)/binfmt.d/ -maxdepth 1 \
    ! -name 'qemu-aarch64.conf' \
    ! -name 'qemu-arm.conf' \
    ! -name 'qemu-riscv64.conf' \
    -type f -exec rm -v {} +

%install_file %(pkgdir)/qemu-guest-agent.service -t %(installroot)/%(libdir)/systemd/system/
%install_file %(pkgdir)/*.preset -t %(installroot)/%(libdir)/systemd/system-preset/
%install_file %(pkgdir)/99-qemu-guest-agent.rules -t %(installroot)/%(libdir)/udev/rules.d/

# TODO: Enable name override in %%tmpfiles macro
mkdir -p %(installroot)%(tmpfilesdir)
echo "d /var/log/qemu-ga 0755 root root -" >> %(installroot)%(tmpfilesdir)/qemu-guest-agent.conf

# TODO: Stop boulder emitting dependencies for these guys
rm -v %(installroot)%(datadir)/qemu/s390*
rm -v %(installroot)%(datadir)/qemu/hppa*

# Provided by EDK2
rm -rv %(installroot)/usr/share/qemu/firmware/ \
       %(installroot)/usr/share/qemu/*.fd \
       %(installroot)/usr/share/qemu/edk2-licenses.txt

# Virtual packages
for i in %(name)-base %(name)-desktop %(name)-full; do
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(docdir)/${i}/
    echo "VIRTUAL" > %(installroot)%(docdir)/${i}/README
done

# Deprecated
%install_dir %(installroot)%(docdir)/%(name)/
echo "DEPRECATED" > %(installroot)%(docdir)/%(name)/README

These clients can either be inside local Qt WebViews or any other, potentially remote, client which supports JavaScript, as long as a communication channel such as WebSocket is available.

Qt WebChannel uses introspection on the QObjects and sends this serialized data to the clients. There, with the help of a small JavaScript library, an object is created which simulates the API of the QObject. Any invokable methods, including slots, can be called as well as properties read and written. Additionally you can connect to signals and register JavaScript callbacks as handlers.

packages.name: rust
packages.description: Rust programming language compiler + tools
packages.setup:
# Ensure that we use the system sqlite3
%patch %(pkgdir)/0001-unbundle-sqlite.patch -d src/tools/cargo
find ./vendor/libsqlite3-sys*/sqlite3/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print

# Remove unused vendored libraries
find ./vendor/curl-sys*/curl/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libffi-sys*/libffi/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libssh2-sys*/libssh2/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libz-sys*/src/zlib{,-ng}/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/openssl-src*/openssl/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libgit2-sys*/libgit2/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print

# Fix bootstrap checking checksums for all the files we just deleted
find vendor -name .cargo-checksum.json -print \
    -exec sed -i.uncheck -e 's/"files":{[^}]*}/"files":{ }/' '{}' '+'

%patch %(pkgdir)/ldd-default.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/libdir.patch
packages.build:
LLVM_VERSION=$(${LLVM_CONFIG} --version)
LLVM_MAJOR="$( cut -d '.' -f 1 <<< "${LLVM_VERSION}" )"
LLVM_LIBDIR=$(${LLVM_CONFIG} --libdir)
COMPILER_RT_DIR="${LLVM_LIBDIR}/clang/${LLVM_MAJOR}/lib/linux"

if [[ " ${PATH[*]} " =~ "ccache" ]]; then
    CCACHE_ENABLE="true"
else
    CCACHE_ENABLE="false"
fi

# build.full-bootstrap=true is necessary to force the build to use the stage 1 rustc to build a stage 2 libstd. We need that for profiling data
# We want some kind of lto enabled so that we get profiling data from it, and thin-lto is much faster to build than full lto.
python ./x.py build \
    --build-dir %(workdir)/build-pgo \
    --config %(pkgdir)/config.toml \
    --jobs %(jobs) \
    --set build.ccache=${CCACHE_ENABLE} \
    --set build.full-bootstrap=true \
    --set rust.lto=thin-local \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-i386.a" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-i386.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-x86_64.a" \
    --rust-profile-generate %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data \
    --stage 2

${LLVM_PROFDATA} merge -output=%(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/rustc-pgo.profdata %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/default_*.profraw

# rust-bootstrap is very inconsistent with the stages of various tools that it wants to build between `dist` and `install`. This
# causes a lot of redundant and unnecessary builds if we attempt to do the build with various stages (IE build the compiler first, then the
# tools, then install it last). To prevent this from happening just let `install` figure out what it wants.
DESTDIR=%(installroot) python3 x.py install \
    --build-dir %(workdir)/build-release \
    --config %(pkgdir)/config.toml \
    --jobs %(jobs) \
    --set build.ccache=${CCACHE_ENABLE} \
    --set build.full-bootstrap=false \
    --set rust.lto=fat \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-i386.a" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-i386.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-x86_64.a" \
    --rust-profile-use %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/rustc-pgo.profdata

install -Dm00644 %(installroot)/etc/bash_completion.d/* -t %(installroot)/usr/share/bash-completion/completions

packages.description: PAM-using login and passwd utilities
packages.install:
%make_install

# Manually install man pages
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(mandir)
cp -r --preserve=timestamps man/man* %(installroot)/%(mandir)/

# Stateless
%install_dir %(installroot)%(vendordir)
mv %(installroot)/etc/login.defs %(installroot)%(vendordir)

# Part of sudo/util-linux
rm -rfv %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/su.1* \
        %(installroot)%(mandir)/man8/sulogin.8*

# Stateless PAM
%install_dir %(installroot)/%(vendordir)
mv %(installroot)/etc/pam.d %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/
# Replace with ours
rm -v %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/pam.d/passwd
for i in passwd chgpasswd chpasswd newusers; do
    %install_file %(pkgdir)/pam.d/$i %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/pam.d/
done
for i in groupadd groupdel groupmod useradd usermod userdel; do
    %install_file %(pkgdir)/pam.d/defaults %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/pam.d/$i
done

# Remove files that conflict with util-linux
# Expect vipw, vigr, newgrp, sg to conflict also at a later point
for file in login nologin chfn chsh; do
    find %(installroot)/usr -wholename "*bin/${file}*" -type f -print -exec rm {} \; # binaries
    find %(installroot)%(vendordir) -name "${file}" -type f -print -exec rm {} \; # pam files
    find %(installroot)%(mandir) -regextype posix-extended -regex ".*/${file}.[0-9]" -type f -print -exec rm {} \; # man pages
done

# Ensure /etc/sub{g,u}id files exist
%tmpfiles "f /etc/subuid 0644 root root -"
%tmpfiles "f /etc/subgid 0644 root root -"

packages.name: slibtool
packages.summary: a surrogate libtool implementation, written in C
packages.description:
`slibtool` is an independent reimplementation of the widely used libtool,
written in C. `slibtool` is designed to be a clean, fast, easy-to-use
libtool drop-in replacement, and is accordingly aimed at package authors,
distro developers, and system integrators. `slibtool` maintains compatibility
with libtool in nearly every aspect of the tool's functionality as well as
semantics, leaving out (or turning into a no-op) only a small number of
features that are no longer needed on modern systems.

Being a compiled binary, and although not primarily written for the sake of
performance, building a package with `slibtool` is often faster than with its
script-based counterpart. The resulting performance gain would normally vary
between packages, and is most noticeable in builds that invoke libtool a large
number of times, and which are characterized by the short compilation duration
of individual translation units.

packages.name: sqlite
packages.description: SQLite is a C-language library that implements a small, fast, self-contained, high-reliability, full-featured, SQL database engine. SQLite is the most used database engine in the world. SQLite is built into all mobile phones and most computers and comes bundled inside countless other applications that people use every day.
packages.setup:
# When this C-preprocessor macro is defined, SQLite includes some additional APIs that provide convenient access to meta-data about tables and queries
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA=1"

# This option enables the SQLITE_DBPAGE virtual table.
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DBPAGE_VTAB=1"

# This option enables the dbstat virtual table.
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DBSTAT_VTAB=1"

# This compile-time option enables the SQLITE_STMT virtual table logic.
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_STMTVTAB=1"

# This option enables the sqlite3_unlock_notify() interface and its associated functionality
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_UNLOCK_NOTIFY=1"

# When this option is present, secure_delete defaults to on
# https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_secure_delete
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_SECURE_DELETE=1"

# This option adds additional logic to the ANALYZE command and to the query planner that can help SQLite to chose a better query plan under certain situations
export CPPFLAGS+=" -DSQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4=1"

# Autotools fix for CC detection
export CC_FOR_BUILD="$CC"

# --enable-session is required for nodejs to use the system sqlite3
# --soname=legacy ensures that the soname is set to the legacy libsqlite3.so.0 value (https://sqlite.org/src/forumpost/5a3b44f510df8ded)
%configure \
    --disable-static \
    --disable-static-cli-shell \
    --enable-fts4 \
    --enable-fts5 \
    --enable-geopoly \
    --enable-rtree \
    --enable-session \
    --soname=legacy \
    $extra_args

x86_64.environment:
# Used by sqlite3 command line
extra_args="--enable-readline"
export CFLAGS+=" -mllvm -vp-counters-per-site=4"
x86_64.workload:
pushd ../ClickBench/sqlite

# Expected to fail
set +o pipefail
zstdcat %(sourcedir)/hits.csv.zst | head -n 5000000 > sample.csv
set -o pipefail

%(workdir)/sqlite3 mydb <create.sql
%(workdir)/sqlite3 mydb '.import --csv sample.csv hits'
wc -c mydb

cat queries.sql | while read query; do
    sync

    echo "$query"
    for i in $(seq 1 3); do
        %(workdir)/sqlite3 mydb <<<"${query}"
    done
done

# This breaks boulder roots

packages.check:
# glibc ships the stateless default; fail if systemd's upstream template drifts from it
if [[ %(target_triple) = i686* ]]; then
    exit 0
fi
if [[ ! -f /usr/share/defaults/nsswitch.conf ]]; then
    echo "error: glibc does not ship /usr/share/defaults/nsswitch.conf"
    exit 1
fi
grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' %(workdir)/factory/templates/nsswitch.conf > nsswitch.upstream
grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' /usr/share/defaults/nsswitch.conf > nsswitch.glibc
diff -u nsswitch.upstream nsswitch.glibc || {
    echo "nsswitch.conf drift: update glibc's /usr/share/defaults/nsswitch.conf to match systemd's factory template"
    exit 1
}

packages.description: Tcl is a powerful but easy to use dynamic programming language suitable for a wide range of uses including web and desktop applications, along with networking, administration, and more.
packages.setup:
# We don't currently need any of these
rm -rf ../pkgs/*

%configure \
    --enable-shared \
    --enable-symbols
packages.install:
%make_install \
    install-libraries install-msgs \
    MANN_INSTALL_DIR=%(mandir)/man3 \
    TCL_LIBRARY=%(datadir)/tcl${_version_major_minor}

cd ../
ln -s tclsh${_version_major_minor} %(installroot)%(bindir)/tclsh

# For linking with `-ltcl`
ln -s libtcl${_version_major_minor}.so %(installroot)%(libdir)/libtcl.so

# Install private headers
mkdir -p %(installroot)/%(includedir)/tcl-private/{generic,unix}
find generic unix -name "*.h" -exec cp -p '{}' %(installroot)/%(includedir)/tcl-private/'{}' ';'
pushd %(installroot)/%(includedir)
for i in *.h ; do
    [ -f %(installroot)/%(includedir)/tcl-private/generic/$i ] && ln -sf ../../$i %(installroot)/%(includedir)/tcl-private/generic ;
done
popd

# Remove build traces and switch to correct private headers dir
sed -i -e "s|$PWD/unix|%(libdir)|; s|$PWD|%(includedir)/tcl-private|" %(installroot)/%(libdir)/tclConfig.sh

# Fix man pages (copied verbatim from the debian rules file for tcl9.0)
cd %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1 && \
cat tclsh.1 | sed -e 's/(n)/(3tcl)/g' > tclsh${_version_major_minor}.1 && \
rm tclsh.1

cd %(installroot)%(mandir)/man3 && \
for f in *.[3n] ; do
    f2="$(echo $f | sed -e 's/\.[3n]/.3tcl/')"
    if [ -L "${f}" ]; then
        l=$(readlink -n "${f}" | sed -e 's/\.[3n]/.3tcl/')
        rm "${f}"
        ln -sf "${l}" "${f2}"
    else
        cat "${f}" | sed -e 's/^\.TH \([^ ]\+\|"[^"]\+"\) [3n]/.TH \1 3tcl/' \
        -e 's/\(Tk_[0-9A-Za-z]*\)(3)/\1(3tk)/g' \
        -e 's/\([A-Z][0-9A-Za-z_]*\)(3)/\1(3tcl)/g' \
        -e 's/send(n)/send(3tk)/g' \
        -e 's/text(n)/text(3tk)/g' \
        -e 's/tk(n)/tk(3tk)/g' \
        -e 's/winfo(n)/winfo(3tk)/g' \
        -e 's/(n)/(3tcl)/g' \
        -e "s/\\N'244'/\\[^o]/g" \
        >"${f2}"
        rm "${f}"
    fi
done

packages.name: thunderbird
packages.description: Thunderbird Email Client
packages.setup:
%patch %(pkgdir)/patches/0001-Fix-Firefox-Thunderbird-envvar-conflicts.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/patches/0002-Add-launchable-to-AppStream-metadata.patch

cp %(pkgdir)/build/mozconfig .
sed -e 's|@@JOBCOUNT@@|%(jobs)|' -e 's|@@LIBDIR@@|%(libdir)|' -i mozconfig

if [ $FULL_BUILD -ne 0 ]; then
    # PGO build, no LTO
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-profile-generate=cross" >> mozconfig
else
    # Might as well do it with LTO
    echo "ac_add_options MOZ_LTO=cross,full" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-lto=cross,full" >> mozconfig
fi

./mach configure
packages.build:
./mach build
if [ $FULL_BUILD -ne 0 ]; then
    ./mach package

    # PGO
    # Much of this taken from https://github.com/chaotic-aur/packages/blob/main/firefox-nightly/PKGBUILD
    env \
        LLVM_PROFDATA=llvm-profdata \
        JARLOG_FILE="${PWD}/jarlog" \
        XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$(mktemp -p $(pwd) -d xdg-runtime-XXXXXX)" \
        LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=true \
        MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_GMP_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_GPU_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_RDD_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_SOCKET_PROCESS_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_UTILITY_SANDBOX=1 \
        MOZ_DISABLE_VR_SANDBOX=1 \
        GTK_A11Y=none \
        NO_AT_BRIDGE=1 \
        MOZ_REMOTE_SETTINGS_DEVTOOLS=1 \
    dbus-run-session \
        wlheadless-run \
            -c weston --width=1920 --height=1080 \
            -- ./mach python build/pgo/profileserver.py

    # Make sure PGO data is present
    stat -c "Profile data found (%%s bytes)" merged.profdata
    test -s merged.profdata
    stat -c "Jar log found (%%s bytes)" jarlog
    test -s jarlog

    # Delete instrumented browser
    ./mach clobber objdir

    # Reset mozconfig
    rm mozconfig && cp %(pkgdir)/build/mozconfig .
    sed -e 's|@@JOBCOUNT@@|%(jobs)|' -e 's|@@LIBDIR@@|%(libdir)|' -i mozconfig

    # Enable LTO
    echo "ac_add_options MOZ_LTO=cross,full" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-lto=cross,full" >> mozconfig

    # PGO
    echo "ac_add_options --enable-profile-use=cross" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --with-pgo-profile-path=${PWD}/merged.profdata" >> mozconfig
    echo "ac_add_options --with-pgo-jarlog=${PWD}/jarlog" >> mozconfig

    ./mach build
fi
packages.install:
DESTDIR=%(installroot) ./mach install

for i in 16 22 24 32 48 128 256; do
    %install_dir %(installroot)/%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/${i}x${i}/apps
    ln -srv %(installroot)/%(libdir)/thunderbird/chrome/icons/default/default${i}.png %(installroot)/%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/${i}x${i}/apps/net.thunderbird.Thunderbird.png
done

%install_file %(pkgdir)/install/thunderbird-symbolic.svg %(installroot)%(datadir)/icons/hicolor/symbolic/apps/thunderbird-symbolic.svg
%install_file %(pkgdir)/install/net.thunderbird.Thunderbird.desktop %(installroot)%(datadir)/applications/net.thunderbird.Thunderbird.desktop
%install_file comm/mail/branding/thunderbird/net.thunderbird.Thunderbird.appdata.xml %(installroot)%(datadir)/metainfo/net.thunderbird.Thunderbird.appdata.xml

%install_file %(pkgdir)/install/distribution.ini %(installroot)%(libdir)/thunderbird/distribution/distribution.ini
%install_file %(pkgdir)/install/prefs.js %(installroot)/%(libdir)/thunderbird/defaults/pref/prefs.js

# Use a wrapper script to configure langpacks
rm -v %(installroot)/%(bindir)/thunderbird
%install_exe %(pkgdir)/install/thunderbird-wrapper.sh %(installroot)/%(bindir)/thunderbird
packages.environment:
# Set this to 1 if you want to create a release build, 0 if you're just doing builds locally for testing purposes

packages.install:
%cargo_install coreutils

%install_dir %(installroot)%(datadir)/zsh/site-functions
%install_dir %(installroot)%(datadir)/fish/vendor_completions.d
%install_dir %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1

for item in $(./%(cargo_target_dir)/coreutils --list); do
    case $item in
        uptime|kill|more|hostname)
            continue
            ;;
        *)
            # Install binaries
            ln -v %(installroot)%(bindir)/coreutils %(installroot)%(bindir)/${item}

            # Breaks ZSH completions
            if [[ $item == "[" ]]; then
                continue
            fi

            # Install completions
            ./%(cargo_target_dir)/uudoc completion ${item} bash > %(installroot)%(datadir)/bash-completion/completions/${item} && [ -s %(installroot)%(datadir)/bash-completion/completions/${item} ] || rm -f %(installroot)%(datadir)/bash-completion/completions/${item}
            ./%(cargo_target_dir)/uudoc completion ${item} zsh > %(installroot)%(datadir)/zsh/site-functions/_${item} && [ -s %(installroot)%(datadir)/zsh/site-functions/_${item} ] || rm -f %(installroot)%(datadir)/zsh/site-functions/_${item}
            ./%(cargo_target_dir)/uudoc completion ${item} fish > %(installroot)%(datadir)/fish/vendor_completions.d/${item}.fish && [ -s %(installroot)%(datadir)/fish/vendor_completions.d/${item}.fish ] || rm -f %(installroot)%(datadir)/fish/vendor_completions.d/${item}.fish

            # Now install manpages
            ./%(cargo_target_dir)/uudoc manpage ${item} > %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/${item}.1 && [ -s %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/${item}.1 ] || rm -f %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/${item}.1
            ;;
    esac
done

declare -a _gnu_utils
# https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/issues/10862
# https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/issues/14549
# TODO: revisit again with v0.13.0
# Upstream patch is not accounting umask 0022 yet, hence use gnu-cp for now
_gnu_utils+=(cp)

# https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/an-update-on-rust-coreutils/80773
# use gnu-coreutils for apps having remaining open TOCTOU (time-of-check to time-of-use) issues
_gnu_utils+=(mv rm rmdir)

for i in ${_gnu_utils[@]}; do
    rm -v %(installroot)%(bindir)/${i}
    ln -sv gnu-${i} %(installroot)%(bindir)/${i}
done

packages.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make LLVM=1 KDIR="%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}" KERNELRELEASE=${_kernel}
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
packages.install:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %install_file v4l2loopback.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
packages.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    kernels+=(${dir##*/})
done

packages.setup:
function cmake_webkitgtk() {
    %cmake \
        -DENABLE_SPEECH_SYNTHESIS=OFF \
        -DPORT=GTK \
        -DUSE_FLITE=OFF \
        -DUSE_LIBBACKTRACE=OFF \
        "$@"
}

# We only want one webdriver binary, so build it in the gtk4 build
cmake_webkitgtk \
    -B gtk41 \
    -DENABLE_WEBDRIVER=OFF \
    -DUSE_GTK4=OFF

cmake_webkitgtk \
    -B gtk6 \
    -DENABLE_WEBDRIVER=ON \
    -DUSE_GTK4=ON
packages.build:
_build_of=0
for b in gtk41 gtk6; do

    # Add which build we are on to the ninja output
    # Make sure to update the number of builds if we add an additional variant
    # I have no idea why we can't use ++ or let bash syntax
    _build_of=$( expr ${_build_of} + 1 )
    export NINJA_STATUS="[${_build_of}/2][%%f/%%t %%es] "

    %ccache_zero
    BUILDDIR=${b}
    env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/${b}" %cmake_build
    %ccache_stats
done
packages.install:
for b in gtk41 gtk6; do
    BUILDDIR=${b}
    %cmake_install
done

packages.name: x265
packages.summary: x265 is an open source HEVC encoder
packages.description: The primary objective of x265 is to become the best H.265/HEVC encoder available anywhere, offering the highest compression efficiency and the highest performance on a wide variety of hardware platforms.
packages.setup:
function x265_common() {
    %cmake \
        -S source \
        -DENABLE_HDR10_PLUS=TRUE \
        "$@"
}
function x265_hdr() {
    x265_common \
        -DENABLE_CLI=FALSE \
        -DENABLE_SHARED=FALSE \
        -DEXPORT_C_API=FALSE \
        -DHIGH_BIT_DEPTH=TRUE \
        "$@"
}

if [ -d ../compat ]; then
    pushd ../compat
    %patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-libstdc-15.patch

    # HDR 10-bit and 12-bit support
    x265_hdr \
        -B build-10
    x265_hdr \
        -B build-12 \
        -DMAIN12=TRUE

    x265_common \
        -DENABLE_SHARED=TRUE \
        -DEXTRA_LIB='x265_main10.a;x265_main12.a' \
        -DEXTRA_LINK_FLAGS='-L .' \
        -DLINKED_10BIT=TRUE \
        -DLINKED_12BIT=TRUE
    popd
fi

%patch %(pkgdir)/ftbfs-libstdc-15.patch

# HDR 10-bit and 12-bit support
x265_hdr \
    -B build-10
x265_hdr \
    -B build-12 \
    -DMAIN12=TRUE

x265_common \
    -DENABLE_SHARED=TRUE \
    -DEXTRA_LIB='x265_main10.a;x265_main12.a' \
    -DEXTRA_LINK_FLAGS='-L .' \
    -DLINKED_10BIT=TRUE \
    -DLINKED_12BIT=TRUE
packages.build:
if [ -d ../compat ]; then
    pushd ../compat
        # 10 and 12-bit
        for i in 10 12; do
            %ccache_zero
            BUILDDIR=build-${i}
            env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/build-${i}" %cmake_build
            %ccache_stats
            ln -srv build-${i}/libx265.a %(builddir)/libx265_main${i}.a
        done

        # Final build
        %ccache_zero
        BUILDDIR=%(builddir)
        env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/%(builddir)" %cmake_build
        %ccache_stats
    popd
fi

# 10 and 12-bit
for i in 10 12; do
    %ccache_zero
    BUILDDIR=build-${i}
    env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/build-${i}" %cmake_build
    %ccache_stats
    ln -srv build-${i}/libx265.a %(builddir)/libx265_main${i}.a
done

# Final build
%ccache_zero
BUILDDIR=%(builddir)
env CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}/%(builddir)" %cmake_build
%ccache_stats
packages.install:
if [ -d ../compat ]; then
    pushd ../compat
        mkdir tmp
        DESTDIR="${PWD}/tmp" cmake --install "%(builddir)" --verbose

        # Only copy the sonames
        %install_dir %(installroot)/%(libdir)
        find ${PWD}/tmp/%(libdir) -name "libx265.so.*" -print -exec mv {} %(installroot)/%(libdir) \;
    popd
fi

%cmake_install

rm -rfv %(installroot)%(libdir)/*.a

packages.setup:
%patch %(pkgdir)/linux-7.3-iops-create-no-flag.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/linux-7.3-bvec-iter-bi-offset.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/linux-cpu-feature-enabled.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/linux-7.3-kthread-init-fs.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/bump-Linux-Maximum-7.3.patch

# Regenerate configure/configure.ac after patching
autoreconf -fi

# config.status runs `$SED` as a command; zfs' configure leaves it unset
sed -i -e 's|\$SED|sed|g' configure

for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    mkdir ${_kernel}

    pushd ${_kernel}
    ../configure \
        --prefix=%(prefix) \
        --with-config=kernel \
        --with-linux=%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/build \
        --with-linux-obj=%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/build \
        KERNEL_ARCH=x86_64 \
        KERNEL_CC=%(cc) \
        KERNEL_LD=%(ld) \
        KERNEL_LLVM=1

    popd
done
packages.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
packages.install:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %make_install \
        INSTALL_MOD_PATH=%(installroot)%(prefix) \
        INSTALL_MOD_DIR=extra/fs/zfs

    # We don't need to build _against_ the kernel modules (yet?)
    rm -rfv %(installroot)/usr/src

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
packages.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    kernels+=(${dir##*/})
done

packages.name: zint
packages.description:
Zint is a C library for encoding data in several barcode variants. The
bundled command-line utility provides a simple interface to the library.
Features of the library:
- Over 50 symbologies including all ISO/IEC standards, like QR codes.
- Unicode translation for symbologies which support Latin-1 and Kanji character sets.
- Full GS1 support including data verification and automated insertion of FNC1 characters.
- Support for encoding binary data including NULL (ASCII 0) characters.
- Health Industry Barcode (HIBC) encoding capabilities.
- Output in PNG, EPS and SVG formats with user adjustable sizes and colors.
- Verification stage for SBN, ISBN and ISBN-13 data.

packages.setup:
# we don't need cmake as a python dependency
sed -r -i '/cmake/d' wrappers/python/pyproject.toml
sed -i 's/pybind11\[global\]/pybind11/' wrappers/python/pyproject.toml

# ZXING_PYTHON_MODULE=ON builds the Python shared library but not the metadata, so we still need to build the wheel with pyproject
%cmake \
    -DSTB_IMAGE_INCLUDE_DIR=%(includedir)/stb \
    -DZXING_C_API=ON \
    -DZXING_EXAMPLES=OFF \
    -DZXING_PYTHON_INSTALL_LIBDIR=%(libdir) \
    -DZXING_PYTHON_MODULE=ON \
    -DZXING_USE_BUNDLED_ZINT=OFF \
    -DZXING_WRITERS=BOTH
packages.install:
%cmake_install

pushd wrappers/python
%pyproject_install
popd

# Substitute the python shared library built by pyproject which is statically linked with the shared one built by cmake
python_version=$(python -c 'import sys; print(".".join(map(str, sys.version_info[:2])))')
pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/python${python_version}/site-packages/zxingcpp/
python_lib=$(find . -type f -iname "zxingcpp.abi3*")
mv -f %(installroot)%(libdir)/${python_lib:2} .
patchelf --remove-rpath ${python_lib}

# Not needed since it's built by the wheel
rm -rfv %(installroot)%(libdir)/*.{py,pyi,typed}
